sections.section_title: Case presentation and early red flags for a telomere biology disorder
sections.description: Summarizes the patient’s longitudinal symptoms and exam, highlighting features that point beyond isolated nutritional deficiency toward a multisystem premature-ageing/telomere biology disorder (TBD).
subtopics: Five-year trajectory of progressive fatigue, functional decline, weight loss, exertional dyspnoea
Examination: pallor, icterus, premature greying, mucosal atrophy (bald tongue), knuckle hyperpigmentation, hepatosplenomegaly, scoliosis, thenar atrophy, decreased breath sounds

Initial labs: pancytopenia with low reticulocyte count, dimorphic RBCs with basophilic stippling, Cabot rings, hypersegmented neutrophils; severe vitamin B12 and folate deficiency; iron/ferritin pattern of ineffective erythropoiesis
Problem representation: young adult with multisystem involvement (cytopenia, neuropathy, osteoporosis, hepatic and pulmonary fibrosis) and premature-ageing stigmata
Early red flags suggesting TBD: age-incongruent organ fibrosis, persistent cytopenia disproportionate to deficiency, premature hair greying/skin changes

sections.section_title: Structured differential and workup of pancytopenia with hepatic and pulmonary fibrosis
sections.description: Details the stepwise evaluation, data interpretation, and exclusion of competing etiologies to narrow toward an inherited marrow-fibrosis syndrome.
subtopics: Differential for pancytopenia: nutritional megaloblastic anemia, aplastic anemia, myelodysplastic neoplasm, autoimmune cytopenias, infiltrative/malignant, infectious, inherited bone marrow failure syndromes/TBD

Bone marrow and cytogenetics: trilineage hematopoiesis with erythroid hyperplasia, increased iron stores, no dysplasia/malignancy; normal karyotype—implications for ineffective erythropoiesis over marrow aplasia/MDS

Hemolysis panel and DAT: elevated LDH and indirect bilirubin; DAT positive (IgG 2+) but low retic and marrow findings argue against immune hemolysis—how to interpret DAT positivity without active hemolysis
Gastrointestinal evaluation: normal endoscopy; duodenal biopsy with parietal cell loss/autoimmune gastritis physiology leading to B12 malabsorption
Hepatic assessment: hepatosplenomegaly, elastography showing steatosis and cirrhosis; negative autoimmune/viral serologies; differential diagnosis of hepatic fibrosis in young adults

Pulmonary findings: HRCT/PET-CT with diffuse ground glass and subpleural fibrotic/atelectatic changes—pattern consistent with early idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) spectrum; differential of ILD in young adults
Role and limitations of PET-CT in unexplained cytopenia and systemic disease

Ancillary abnormalities: secondary hyperparathyroidism, hypocalcaemia/hypokalaemia, vitamin D deficiency, osteoporosis on DXA; EMG/NCS showing asymmetric axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy—attribution to B12 deficiency versus TBD

sections.section_title: Telomere biology disorders and PARN: focused mechanisms and phenotype correlations
sections.description: Provides the essential pathophysiology needed to contextualize this case, emphasizing how PARN dysfunction shortens telomeres and produces the observed organ involvement.
subtopics: Telomere structure-function and attrition; telomerase complex (TERT, TERC) in telomere maintenance
PARN biology: deadenylation of RNAs; role in 3′-end maturation of TERC and stabilization of telomerase RNP; expected consequence of reduced PARN activity on telomere length
Genotype–phenotype spectrum: biallelic PARN variants (DKCB6, severe TBD including HH) versus monoallelic variants (pulmonary fibrosis and/or bone marrow failure—PFBMFT4)
Organ tropism in TBD: bone marrow failure risk, pulmonary and hepatic fibrosis, mucocutaneous and skeletal manifestations, premature greying—mapping to the patient’s findings
Modifier effects and incomplete penetrance: environmental and physiologic stressors (for example, severe B12 deficiency) unmasking hematopoietic vulnerability in TBD
Expected laboratory and imaging signatures in PARN-related disease and how this case aligns with expanding literature

sections.section_title: Diagnostic synthesis and genetic variant interpretation in suspected TBD
sections.description: Explains how clinicians unified disparate findings, when to order genetic and telomere testing, and how to handle a Variant of Uncertain Significance in PARN.
subtopics: From disparate clues to a unifying diagnosis: reconciling persistent cytopenia, premature-ageing features, and dual-organ fibrosis in a young adult
Indications for genetic testing and telomere length measurement (flow-FISH) in multisystem, age-incongruent disease
Exome result: monoallelic PARN c.613T>C (p.Cys205Arg) in the R3H domain—conservation and predicted deleteriousness
Applying ACMG/AMP criteria to this variant (PM1, PM2, PP2, PP3) and why it remains a VUS
Clinical management of a VUS: segregation studies, functional assays, repeat classification over time, and proceeding with a clinical TBD diagnosis when phenotype and gene fit
Counselling points: variable penetrance, potential de novo occurrence, somatic genetic rescue/mosaicism, and implications for cascade testing of relatives

sections.section_title: Management, surveillance, and prognosis in PARN-related telomere biology disorders
sections.description: Outlines immediate care for this patient and general principles for longitudinal management of PARN-associated TBDs, including organ-specific monitoring and when to escalate to disease-modifying interventions.
subtopics: Acute and supportive care in this case: parenteral B12 regimen, folate, transfusion support, vitamin D/calcium repletion, electrolyte correction, physiotherapy
Hematologic follow-up: CBC/reticulocyte monitoring, triggers for repeat marrow evaluation, early referral for HSCT evaluation in evolving marrow failure; reduced-intensity conditioning nuances in TBD
Pulmonary management: baseline and serial PFTs and HRCT; consideration of antifibrotics in IPF phenotype; transplant timing and outcomes in short telomere syndromes
Hepatic management: elastography intervals, portal hypertension screening, transplant considerations; avoidance of hepatotoxic agents and alcohol moderation
Potential disease-modifying options: androgens (danazol, nandrolone)—indications, monitoring, risks; investigational therapies aimed at telomere maintenance
Risk mitigation: avoid myelotoxic drugs and unnecessary radiation; smoking cessation; vaccination and infection prophylaxis
Genetic counselling, psychosocial support, and reproductive options

Prognosis and this patient’s early outcome: initial symptomatic and hematologic improvement with deficiency correction; need for lifelong surveillance for marrow failure, progressive ILD, hepatic decompensation, and malignancy
